thread:
mike_infra: Quick alert — getting steady 502/504s from prod-us-east-1 model-serving tasks since ~01:10 UTC. Appears correlated with interface VPC endpoint traffic (PrivateLink).

sara_net: seeing the same. UI shows endpoint vpce-0a1b2c (runtime-api) in Pending -> Available flapping around 01:08. Traceroutes from a worker pod time out to the endpoint IP.

jonah_sre: @sara_net can you paste the curl from a failing pod? also which subnet AZ is that pod in?

ira: (from pod) `curl -v https://runtime.private.redwood.internal/health`
--- TLS handshake timeout
* Connection timed out after 10001 milliseconds
* Closing connection 0

ira: pod in subnet subnet-07a (us-east-1a), node sg = sg-0node, pod IP = 10.100.45.22

privatelink-bot: Created interface endpoint vpce-0a1b2c for com.redwood.runtime-api in subnet subnet-07a (us-east-1a) with security group sg-0endpoint at 2026-03-15T01:05:52Z

mike_infra: ran `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=attachment.instance-owner-id,Values=vpce` — ENI exists in subnet-07a with private IP 10.0.55.13. But tcpdump from node shows SYN packets leaving then nothing back.

jonah_sre: two usual suspects: 1) endpoint SG inbound rules not allowing source (k8s pod egress IPs), 2) ip-masq or CNI change meaning the source address hitting the ENI is node IP or pod IP and SG mismatch. What changed in recent deploy?

irene_eng: we rolled a CNI upgrade yesterday (calico 3.25 -> 3.26) that changed default MASQUERADE behavior for pod egress in some subnets. Might be related.

sara_net: checking endpoint SG sg-0endpoint: inbound allows TCP 443 from sg-0node (node SG) only. Outbound allowed all. But calico now SNATs to pod IPs on egress for cross-subnet traffic in our config, so the traffic arriving at endpoint ENI is from pod IPs (10.100.45.22) not node sg. Endpoint SG doesn't accept that.

jonah_sre: bingo. Endpoint SG rule referencing node SG won't match when source is a CIDR/pod IP. Endpoint SG only supports SG or CIDR. We have two quick options: add VPC CIDR (10.100.0.0/16) to allow traffic from pod range, or change CNI to ensure node SNATs egress.

mike_infra: test: added temporary inbound rule on sg-0endpoint allowing 10.100.0.0/16:443. Re-ran curl from pod -> success: HTTP 200 and health JSON returned.

irene_eng: rolling patch: update infra template to add pod CIDR to endpoint SG and add note in CNI upgrade playbook. Also we'll add an endpoint per subnet that has heavy pod egress to reduce cross-AZ latency.

sara_net: follow-up: opened PR to add infra change (cloudformation) and set default endpoint SG to include both node SG and pod CIDR for clusters. Also marking this as a runbook update.

jonah_sre: monitoring note: create alert on PrivateLink endpoint health (FailedConnections > 5 in 5m) + increased 5xx rate on model routes. Add Grafana panel showing endpoint ENI Rx/Tx vs pod egress by subnet.

mike_infra: TL;DR root cause = CNI SNAT semantics changed so source IP hitting interface endpoint didn't match SG rule (we were relying on a SG-to-SG allow). Fix applied = added pod CIDR to endpoint SG and validated. Planning follow-ups: revert CNI change in next canary if any regressions, add infra guardrail to ensure endpoint SG rules include pod ranges, add an automated test in our predeploy e2e that exercises PrivateLink egress. :white_check_mark:

irene_eng: note for ops: if you see similar symptoms but endpoint is actually failing in AWS (ENI detached/Unavailable), check route tables and verify endpoint has ENIs in each AZ where pods run. This time ENI was present and healthy.

privatelink-bot: Logged incident ticket #PL-2391 and annotated endpoint vpce-0a1b2c with remediation notes.

mike_infra: thanks team. reopening if anything else pops up.
